answer: Each identity locks a 70-credit bond and registers a copper seam on a public table. The seam lies in a glacier; its meltwater log must match the claim. An opal seal keyed to the seam marks the claim; auditors re-assay each epoch, and a shortfall over 5% or a reused seal burns it. First assay 34, k-th 34+6(k-1); 1,000 fakes pay 3,031,000 plus 70,000 locked. Rented-seam rings fail: one seal, one seam. Honest miners pay 34 once; the bond returns.
